title: HVAC load-calculation professional workflow
finding: Project criteria and architectural/BIM/CAD inputs → space/zone decomposition → design climate/indoor criteria → envelope/fenestration → gains and schedules → ventilation/infiltration → review inputs → room/zone loads → peak/coincident system analysis → psychrometrics/sizing → QA → issued calculations → downstream design.

title: Occupational knowledge to automation research
finding: Original Atlas identities cooling_loads and hvac_design; interfaces cad_automation, bim_automation, engineering_software, workflow_automation and data_automation. Implementation exploration cannot redefine Atlas authority.

title: Legacy DWG to HAP route
finding: DWG extraction, engineering review, source-backed candidates, approval, Excel/guide and manual HAP entry form the historical intended workflow, not demonstrated end-to-end capability or approved architecture.

title: Egypt source families
finding: HBRC Code 306/2005 listing, dedicated air-conditioning/refrigeration code family, HBRC/BUILD_ME performance tool. Editions, clauses and applicability must be confirmed. Hourly energy analysis is distinct from peak sizing.

title: Source authority roles
finding: Historical baseline references ASHRAE/ACCA 183-2024, ASHRAE 169-2025, 2025 Fundamentals chapters 14–19, CIBSE Guide A, textbook/training and HAP implementation. These serve different procedural, technical, pedagogical and software-evidence roles. No new source verification.

title: Alternatives to custom AutoCAD integration
finding: Prior research cites Carrier gbXML, Revit analytical models/export/API, gbXML schema, TRACE 3D Plus and IES VE workflows. Public HAP automation API remains unproven; compare existing supported workflows before choosing build/integrate/adapt/manual.

title: Exchange compatibility
finding: Historical research identifies Revit 2026 export gbXML 7.03 versus then-current schema 8.01. 'Supports gbXML' does not prove semantic transfer or consumer compatibility. Version-specific findings require recheck at implementation.

title: Controlled transfer experiment
finding: Use small controlled model with known authoritative fields; track identity/revision/units; separately assess geometry and properties; record defaults, transformed and missing values. Import success is not data validity.

title: Engineering data provenance
finding: Maintain acquisition status, source reference, modification audit and approval independently. Source types include standard, code, manufacturer, research, project document and engineer input; no confidential or unauthorized source files.

title: Value authority and special review
finding: No invented engineering values; trace unit, source edition/locator, confidence, design stage and approval. Preliminary values require engineer review; critical medical spaces specialist review.

title: EngineeringValue<T> implementation
finding: Nullable value and separate data, approval, confidence, provenance and design-stage fields; default NotAvailable/NotReviewed/Low; computed approval/preliminary flags are separate. Class alone does not enforce source completeness.

title: Unit-test coverage
finding: Six tests cover preliminary nonapproval, approved value flag, standard-suggested preliminary flag, Egypt default, operating-room specialist marker and core assembly independence from Autodesk. Read test source; did not execute tests.

title: Actual prototype boundary
finding: THDATA0 selects a closed 2D polyline of at least three vertices and prints area in square drawing units. Does not perform unit conversion, load calculation, multi-space extraction or HAP transfer in this command.

title: Research before implementation
finding: Keep old AutoCAD→Plugin→HAP candidate as evidence; define problem, source/data contract, compare alternatives and empirical evidence before architecture choice. Avoid treating code existence as professional product approval.
